subsystems.name: Solid electrolyte
subsystems.role: replaces the flammable liquid electrolyte; conducts lithium ions and physically blocks dendrites

subsystems.name: Anode
subsystems.role: stores lithium during charging; often lithium metal for high energy density
parts: lithium metal foil or silicon composite

subsystems.name: Cathode
subsystems.role: releases lithium during charging; sets voltage and capacity
parts: layered oxide or other active material

subsystems.name: Cell stack and packaging
subsystems.role: assembles anode, electrolyte and cathode into a sealed cell

subsystems.name: Battery management system
subsystems.role: monitors and protects the pack; balances cells and estimates state of charge

subsystems.name: Power conversion and interface
subsystems.role: for a power bank, converts battery voltage to standard USB outputs

buildSteps.title: Make the solid electrolyte
buildSteps.detail: Ceramic powders such as garnet-type are synthesised, milled and sintered into dense membranes; polymer electrolytes are cast from solution. Sulfide electrolytes are handled in dry rooms because they react with moisture.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Cathode slurry is coated onto aluminium foil and dried. Lithium metal foil is laminated onto copper foil for the anode. Both are cut to size.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the cells
buildSteps.detail: Anode, solid electrolyte and cathode are stacked and pressed. Ceramic cells may be co-sintered at high temperature; polymer cells are laminated. The stack is sealed in a pouch or prismatic can.

buildSteps.title: Form and test cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells undergo initial charge-discharge cycles to form stable interfaces, then are tested for capacity, impedance and safety.

buildSteps.title: Build the pack
buildSteps.detail: Cells are connected in series and parallel to give the required voltage and capacity, and fitted into a mechanical frame with thermal pads.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the BMS
buildSteps.detail: Sensors and balancing electronics are wired to each cell group, and firmware is loaded to manage charging, discharging and protection.

buildSteps.title: Add power conversion
buildSteps.detail: DC-DC converters and USB-C PD controllers are connected to the pack, along with a charger input and user interface.

buildSteps.title: Test and certify
buildSteps.detail: The finished power bank is tested for capacity, efficiency, drop, thermal and safety standards before shipping.

prerequisites.tech: Solid electrolytes with high ionic conductivity
prerequisites.why: ceramic and sulfide electrolytes exist but still need better conductivity, stability and low-cost manufacturing.
lithium metal anodes are used in labs but dendrite formation and interface resistance remain challenges at scale.
pilot lines exist, but high-volume, low-cost production is not yet mature, especially for ceramics.
BMS technology is well established, though solid-state cells have different voltage and temperature characteristics.
standards for solid-state batteries are still being developed, especially for transport and consumer use.

pathway.milestone: small solid-state cells in wearables and specialty devices; early power banks marketed as solid-state, often using semi-solid or polymer electrolytes
pathway.unlocks: first consumer exposure and validation of safety claims.

pathway.milestone: pilot production of ceramic and sulfide cells for premium electronics
pathway.unlocks: higher energy density power banks and thinner devices.

pathway.milestone: cost reduction through scaling and automation
pathway.unlocks: mainstream adoption in phones, laptops and power banks.

pathway.milestone: solid-state batteries in electric vehicles and grid storage
pathway.unlocks: faster charging, longer life and improved safety at large scale.
